sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
ANB Metal Cast Limited; NSE SME; ISIN INE0VG001016. Research cutoff 2026-10-20. Dated quote ₹340.0 on 2026-10-19, not a live executable bid. Five-year nominal INR scenarios use a 15% analyst equity hurdle and ₹5 lakh illustrative position. Current scope and capital bridge are described in financial forensics and the linked model.

Gate conclusions: G 1 Integrity: Historical connected-property arms-length/compliance uncertainty is explicitly disclosed; GOV 4, not an automatic integrity-failure allegation. G 2 Financial reliability: Share, premium, debt and latest three-year cash bridges resolved. Current volume decomposition and unspecified advances remain analytical limits, not proven false accounts. G 3 Funding: Rating reports adequate liquidity, but linked stress requires new borrowing; access beyond committed facilities is not assumed. No proven current default or automatic G 3 failure. G 4 Tradability: Dated NSE quote/lot and observed liquidity checked; spreads, circuits, restrictions and executable depth remain unverified.

Evidence confidence: financial_levels: high; cash_classification: medium; governance: medium; economic_growth: insufficient for REV; reported revenue high confidence; funding_model: medium as requirement estimates; actual facilities unconfirmed; overall_weakest_material: insufficient for composite scores. Forecast uncertainty is distinct from accuracy of the underlying disclosures.

Official 2026-10-19 close ₹340.0; volume 6,000.0 shares, turnover ₹2,034,680, 15.0 trades, lot 400, series ['SM']. This dated trade is not a live executable bid. 20-session mean/median daily turnover ₹14,703,619/₹5,700,770; conservative denominator is the lower. ₹5 lakh theoretical exit takes 4.39/1.75/0.88 sessions at 2%/5%/10% participation before whole-lot rounding. 60-session window has 58 observed and 2 absent sessions; no zero-filled liquidity conclusion until listing dates/missing records are reconciled. Not an exit guarantee: spreads, available bids, circuits, impact, settlement/surveillance and whole-lot minimum positions remain to be checked. [M1]

No ISIN match in the checked NSE ESM/ASM lists dated 20 October and GSM list dated 19 October. This is not blanket clearance from all restrictions or proof of executable liquidity. Other exchange measures, price bands, settlement series and live spreads still require review.

Official October 19 EOD indicators, effective next trading session October 21: Less than 100 unique PAN traded in previous 30 days; SME scrip is not regularly traded. These cautions do not contradict the actual observed turnover history: generic irregular-trading status is not evidence of any particular missing session. PAN breadth and expired mandatory market-making can weaken executable depth even when daily turnover is present. [REG1][REGFMT]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: FY 26/FY 25 revenue ₹225.1908/162.5686 cr; PAT ₹21.4596/10.2471 cr; EPS ₹20.15/11.87. FY 26 CFO is −₹39.1780 cr, with receivables absorbing ₹32.0035 cr and inventory ₹37.5176 cr. Cash fixed-asset purchases ₹6.0953 cr imply FCF proxy −₹45.2733 cr. This is a cash-intensive growth profile, not proof that headline profit is fictitious. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Top ten customers were 87.00% of FY 24 sales and 93.41% in the five months to August 2024; top one was 18.14% and 20.85%. These are historical figures, not asserted FY 26 concentration. The prospectus compares Maan Aluminium and Banco Products, but Banco is consolidated with different products and scale; December 2024 peer prices cannot anchor an October 2026 valuation. Aluminium pass-through mitigates input-price risk while obscuring demand growth: conversion margin per tonne, actual extrusion tonnes, recovery/yield and customer credit deserve more weight than revenue alone. Credit evidence reports 90–120-day customer terms and advance purchasing, explaining why profitable volume growth can consume cash. [P1][U1]

Maan Aluminium management separately reported Q 3 FY 26 manufacturing sales growth of 10% but trading sales decline around 32%. This illustrates why gross metal revenue is not a clean demand measure. Its manufacturing/trading mix, larger plant and export exposure differ from AMCL, so neither its margin nor historic prospectus P/E is copied into a fair-value target. [PEER1]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Draft-prospectus restated FY 22/FY 23/FY 24 revenues are ₹51.3399/84.2746/112.1205 cr and PAT ₹0.4190/1.8463/5.3363 cr. FY 25/FY 26 annual-report revenue ₹162.5686/225.1908 cr and PAT ₹10.2471/21.4596 cr extend the operating history. FY 23–26 reported sales CAGR is 38.8%; metal-price pass-through and extrusion volume must be separated before assigning REV mechanically. FY 22/FY 23/FY 24 CFO was −₹4.2965/−6.3990/−7.2960 cr. FY 26 CFO −₹39.1780 cr therefore is not the first negative operating-cash year. FY 25 CFO ₹3.9962 cr is now verified in the final prospectus; the complete latest three-year conversion is shown below. FY 22–24 cumulative CFO/PAT = −17.9915/7.6016 = −2.367. This demonstrates historical growth funding dependence, not fictitious sales. [P1][S1]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Operating EBIT excluding other income is FY 26 ₹31.6270 cr versus FY 25 ₹16.5552 cr. At a standardized 25% tax, FY 26 NOPAT is ₹23.72025 cr. Total equity plus debt rose from ₹68.2993 cr to ₹147.0807 cr; NOPAT over average total capital is 22.03%, while incremental NOPAT/added capital is 14.35%. These proxies are not commodity-cycle-normalized or mature-cohort returns. The significant IPO capital and delayed cash realization make a high reported ROCE insufficient proof of value-creating reinvestment. [S1]

March 2026 inventory ₹70.1517 cr plus receivables ₹67.7006 cr exceeds the prior-year ₹32.6341+35.6970 cr by ₹69.5212 cr. Gross bank/other borrowings in balance-sheet long/short lines are ₹47.4468 cr, with cash ₹9.0511 cr; the rating debt total ₹48.74 cr uses a different perimeter/adjustment and is not silently substituted. Advances ₹7.2904 cr and other current assets ₹7.8077 cr also tie up funds. The ₹42.9114 cr net IPO helped fund expansion but did not eliminate debt dependence. At unchanged FY 26 revenue, another 30 days of receivables alone would tie up about ₹18.51 cr, more than reported cash. A 10% inventory impairment is ₹7.02 cr before tax, versus FY 26 PAT ₹21.46 cr. These are mechanical stresses, not predictions. Facility headroom, collateral and repayment maturity decide whether the combined stress causes new equity funding. [S1][U1]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
AZ Windows is described as 65%-owned by the promoter; connected sales, prices and credit terms warrant monitoring. The ₹39.7114 cr financing-reserve line and current share count are reconciled in financial forensics, rather than treated as recurring subsidy or left as unresolved dilution. [S1]

Acuité18 September rationale assignedBBB/Stable to₹59 cr facilities. Gross-current-asset days 263 versus 187, inventory 133 versus 82 and debtors 110 versus 81 confirm cash absorption beyond sales growth; extended customer credit 90–120 days and upfront procurement explain the mechanism. FY 26 debt₹48.74 cr versus₹34.33 cr; net IPOproceeds₹42.91 cr, newFY 27 working-capital termloan₹8.76 cr and proposedcapexdebt₹5 cr. Rating calls liquidity adequate: averagebankutilization 78.98%, cash₹9.05 cr, FY 26 cashaccrual₹22.28 cr versus termrepayment₹1.32 cr. Cashaccrual is not CFO and excludes working-capital absorption; forecastaccrual is not verifiedcash. Aluminium pricepass-through mitigates, not eliminates, inventoryrisk. [U1]

Historical connected land purchases total ₹0.978 cr from Pivot Production FY 23 and ₹0.90 cr each from Confiance/Ornate FY 24. Prospectus risk factor 15 explicitly declines assurance on arms-length terms/compliance, a real unresolved governance issue rather than just generic boilerplate approval. FY 25 connected AZ Windows sales ₹5.3668 cr and purchases ₹0.0608 cr are actual flows, unlike approval ceilings. CFO Sagar Asodariya resigned September 7 citing relocation and no other material reason; Hussain Harif Khan appointed September 8. The board also proposed ANB Limited name, conditional on statutory approval: do not assume the legal rename is effective. [P2][CFO][S1]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The share-capital roll-forward resolves the old-share-label error: 8,634,780 opening shares plus 3,200,000 issued equals 11,834,780 closing shares. Face value ₹10 gives ₹11.83478 cr capital. Promoter Avnish Gajera retained 7,899,990 shares; percentage fell 91.49% to 66.75% because the denominator expanded, not necessarily promoter selling. Securities premium added ₹46.72 cr less ₹7.0086 cr issue costs = ₹39.7114 cr, exactly the cash-flow line labeled Subsidy & Other Reserve. Adding ₹3.20 cr new share capital gives ₹42.9114 cr net IPO proceeds. These two primary-note bridges remove the preliminary financial-reliability concern; neither discrepancy independently supports a G 2 hold. At ₹340 and the closing share count, indicative equity value is ₹402.38 cr; FY 26 PAT/share on closing capital is ₹18.13, versus weighted reported EPS ₹20.15, so dilution-aware trailing P/E is about 18.75 x. Check post-March changes before treating this as the current fully diluted value. [S1][M1]

Final prospectus supplies FY 25 CFO ₹3.9962 cr. FY 24 summary CFO −₹7.2960 cr differs from risk-panel −₹7.3029 cr by only ₹0.0069 cr; this rounding/classification-level difference cannot overturn the conclusion. Three-year CFO/PAT is −1.147. FY 26 investing includes ₹7.2691 cr advances and ₹7.3824 cr other assets as well as capex; reported CFO therefore does not capture all operating-like funding absorption. Other current liabilities contain ₹1.2931 cr current debt maturities: adding these to long/short borrowings reconciles exactly to ₹48.7399 cr, matching the rounded credit figure. [P2][S1][U1]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At ₹340 and 11.83478 m shares, current-share trailing P/E is about 18.75 x. Conditional base/bear/bull model IRRs are 2.00%/-42.04%/23.15%; terminal prices ₹375.37/₹22.24/₹963.11. Base 15%-hurdle entry arithmetic ₹186.62 is conditional, not a recommendation. Additional funding required is shown annually, including settlement of opening tax liability and the subsequent ECGLS loan; unapproved debt is not represented as available. IAS remains NS because Q is incomplete and actual funding under stress is not demonstrated. [S1][U1][P2][M1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Analyst stress: aluminium-price reversal reduces inventory realizations while customers delay payment, funding needs rise and extrusion margins compress. Track tonnes and conversion margin, aged inventories, customer/related-party receipts, cash-credit headroom, and proceeds deployment. Three-year cash and ownership bridges are now reconstructed. Composite scores remain NS because current volume/price decomposition is unavailable; linked funding/valuation stresses and supported partial factors are below.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-times/ten-times ₹340 means ₹1,700/₹3,400 after five years. At an assumed 15 x terminal earnings multiple and unchanged closing shares, required PAT is ₹134.13/268.25 cr, versus ₹21.46 cr FY 26, approximately 44.3%/65.7% annual profit growth. At unchanged 9.53% PAT margin, revenue would need about ₹1,408/2,815 cr, far beyond demonstrated installed capacity and funding. These are reverse requirements, not forecasts; no supported multibagger claim follows. [S1][P2][M1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Monitor extrusion tonnes, realization and conversion margin per tonne; 9,800 MT versus proposed 12,000 MT capacity; receivable/inventory days 110/133; cumulative cash realization; ₹7.29 cr unspecified advances and ₹5.87 cr supplier advances; AZ Windows terms/receipts; cash-credit utilization; opening tax settlement; debt after the ₹8.76 cr loan; CFO reporting continuity. Acuité downside indicators include cash accrual below ₹15 cr, unexpected debt growth and longer working-capital cycle. These are rating sensitivities, not automatic equity triggers. [S1][U1][P2]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Fast-growing aluminium extrusion company whose IPO and borrowing funded inventory and customer credit rather than free cash. Operating capacity and profit progress are real, but historical connected land dealings, persistent cash absorption and missing current volume/price decomposition prevent a clean compounder or ranked investment conclusion. Completed source-led review with explicit NS composites. REV is unscoreable because metal pass-through and missing FY 26 tonnes obscure economic growth. BQS has 88% coverage; GQS 60%, with persistent CASH 3 implying cap 5 if completed. Missing factors are not renormalized.

Final published measures: BQS NS; GQS NS; IAS NS. Any change in price, funded cash deployment, share count or execution restrictions requires recomputation; these are conditional research classifications, not a trade instruction.

Facts, calculations, management claims and assumptions are distinguished in the evidence audit. REV remains NS: no FY 26 volume/price/mix bridge in reviewed primary sources; reported sales growth is not assumed organic demand. Historical connected-property terms and current unspecified advances need independent economic substantiation. valuation.status: Conditional linked funding stress; IAS remains NS because growth-quality factor and financing availability are unresolved
assumption_basis: March debt includes current maturities embedded in other liabilities; this reconciles precisely to Acuité ₹48.74cr. Subsequent ₹8.76cr loan is added to debt without assuming its proceeds remain unspent.

The full opening income-tax provision ₹9.6057cr is settled in the model, because this is a liability outstanding before forecast taxes. Duties/tax assets remain in working capital; immediate offset would reduce funding needs, but its availability is not assumed. ₹5cr operating reserve is excluded from distributable cash.

Base 12% sales growth is below historical reported growth, with 14% EBIT approximating FY26 operating margin. Lack of current tonnes/price split makes it an estimate, not proven demand. Bear 7% and severe 3% margins stress metal/conversion economics.

Working capital begins with disclosed stock, receivables, advances and other current assets net of operating liabilities, excluding debt and tax provisions. Forward 57%/70%/45% ratios model base/bear/bull collection discipline.

Capex is at least ₹8cr in year one and 3% of sales thereafter, depreciation 0.4%, debt interest 9%, tax 25% on positive PBT, principal repayment ₹2.1cr annually. No dividends or new equity assumed. Additional debt is a funding REQUIREMENT, not evidence facilities are available.
Exit 10/12/16 times operating NOPAT less debt plus cash is an analyst sensitivity. Severe 8x. Gross proceeds and retained cash are not counted twice.

GOV.reason: Promoter controls 66.75%; final prospectus explicitly cannot assure historical related-party land purchases were arms-length or fully compliant. AZ Windows sales were ₹5.3668cr in FY25 and approval expands a promoter-controlled relationship. This warrants a below-average governance assessment, not an unsupported fraud finding; current actual terms remain unverified.

MOAT.reason: Extrusion capacity, tooling and customer relationships provide useful access, but competitive organised/unorganised supply and pass-through pricing limit structural bargaining power. Historical top-ten concentration is high.

REV.reason: Reported FY23–26 CAGR 38.8% is verified, but FY25 production rose 13.0% against revenue 45.0%. Current production/price/mix bridge is unavailable. Pass-through materially obscures demand, so v3 requires REV NS rather than a mechanical high score.

DUR.reason: Capacity utilization and qualified applications offer growth opportunity; 9,800 MT rated current capacity is below the originally illustrated 12,000 MT annual expansion endpoint. Customer concentration and extended credit limit durable growth.

CAP.reason: Operating EBIT excluding other income is FY26 ₹31.6270cr versus FY25 ₹16.5552cr. At a standardized 25% tax, FY26 NOPAT is ₹23.72025cr. Total equity plus debt rose from ₹68.2993cr to ₹147.0807cr; NOPAT over average total capital is 22.03%, while incremental NOPAT/added capital is 14.35%. These proxies are not commodity-cycle-normalized or mature-cohort returns. The significant IPO capital and delayed cash realization make a high reported ROCE insufficient proof of value-creating reinvestment. Broad cash returns remain much weaker than accounting returns.

CASH.reason: FY24/FY25/FY26 CFO −₹7.2960/+3.9962/−39.1780cr versus PAT ₹5.3363/10.2471/21.4596cr gives cumulative −42.4778/37.0430=−1.147. FY25 improvement is contrary evidence, but FY22/23 were also negative; persistent cash realization weakness is established. FY26 advances/other assets additionally consume cash in investing classification.

BAL.reason: Acuité BBB/Stable reports adequate liquidity and 78.98% average utilization, contrary to a default claim. However debt rises after IPO, stock/debtor concentration is high and modeled stress requires funding; bank approval is not assumed.

EXEC.reason: Production increased from 3,360 MT FY23 to 6,100 FY25 and current capacity is 9,800 MT, but cash conversion deteriorated and the 12,000 MT planned endpoint is not confirmed. CFO resignation cites relocation, with next-day replacement, not alleged accounting objections.

EARN.reason: FY26 profit growth is supported mainly by higher material/conversion margin and limited other income, but weighted EPS overstates current-share earnings and weak cash realization reduces certainty that profits become distributable. This factor evaluates earnings composition, distinct from the CASH score.
